chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Amr ibn al-Miqdam from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was in Kufa, among you, going out early every morning from the palace, touring the markets of Kufa, one market after another, and with him was the staff on his shoulder, which had two ends and was called 'al-sabibah'. So he would stop by the people of each market and call out: 'O assembly of merchants, fear Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

When they heard his voice, they would drop what was in their hands, direct their hearts to him, and listen with their ears. So he would say: 'Advance goodness, seek blessings in ease, draw near to the buyers and sellers, adorn yourselves with forbearance, refrain from oaths, avoid lying, keep away from oppression, do justice to the oppressed, and do not approach usury.'
And give full measure and weight.
And do not deprive people of their things and do not spread corruption in the earth.
So he would tour all the markets in Kufa, then return and sit for the people.

key_terms.اَلدِّرَّةُ: a staff or cane carried by the Imam
key_terms.اَلسَّبِيبَةُ: the name given to the Imam's two-ended staff

ai.seo_question: What ethical guidelines did Imam Ali provide for merchants in the markets of Kufa?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) active governance model, where he personally inspected the Kufa markets to ensure justice and prevent exploitation. The specific mention of the *Sabibah* (a double-ended staff) symbolizes his readiness to administer discipline while his sermons integrated spiritual piety with commercial ethics, such as avoiding *Riba* and ensuring fair weights. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly view that leadership involves direct engagement with the economic welfare of the community.
